headline: In Indiana, basketball is a religion, and the brick fieldhouse is the church
summary: Indiana's hoops identity lives in high school gyms, the Hoosiers myth and the IU-Purdue split, with Indianapolis as the hub. The Pacers sit on top, with Tyrese Haliburton back from his Achilles tear and the Fever sharing Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Locals dress plain, in college colors and school-gym nostalgia. Honor the gym and the small-town school before the big-city streetball myth.

insights.title: The fieldhouse is the cathedral
insights.detail: Hinkle Fieldhouse at Butler, the 1954 Milan title behind the film Hoosiers and small-town gyms like New Castle's (among the largest high school gyms anywhere) anchor the state's faith. The 2026 Emirates NBA Cup final is at Hinkle on Dec 11.
insights.implication: Build a Hinkle-week capsule around brick, hardwood and rafters and banners. Make the gym, not a logo, the hero graphic.

insights.title: Crispus Attucks is a story to credit, not borrow
insights.detail: Indianapolis's Crispus Attucks High School, with Oscar Robertson, won the 1955 and 1956 state titles. It was the first all-Black school to win the tournament, in a segregated city. It is a point of pride in Black Indianapolis and a piece of civil-rights history.
insights.implication: Partner with the school, its alumni and community institutions on any Attucks product, and pay and credit them. Don't use its marks without a license.

insights.title: Two college religions, one state
insights.detail: Indiana (cream and crimson, Assembly Hall) and Purdue, in black and old gold at Mackey Arena, split the state. Butler, Notre Dame and Indiana State (Larry Bird's school) share the pride. Locals pick a side early and keep it.
insights.implication: Pacers navy and gold overlaps with Purdue's old gold, so avoid colorways that read as college product. Check licensing on any college reference.

insights.title: Mr. Basketball and the All-Star series are the local draft
insights.detail: The Indiana Mr. Basketball award and the Indiana-Kentucky All-Star series are annual rituals that locals follow like a pro draft. The state has produced Eric Gordon, Mike Conley Jr., Greg Oden and Zach Randolph.
insights.implication: Seasonal drops and player stories can draw on the Mr. Basketball lineage. Name-and-likeness uses need athlete agreements.

insights.title: Haliburton's comeback is the new local legend
insights.detail: Tyrese Haliburton returns from the Game 7 Achilles tear to lead a team coming off a 19-63 year, with Siakam, Nembhard, Nesmith and new center Ivica Zubac. Purdue point guard Braden Smith joined on a two-way deal, which ties college loyalty to the pro team.
insights.implication: Lead with resilience and return, in guard-oriented product. Treat the Purdue tie as a hometown-hoops storyline.

insights.title: Indiana is a women's basketball market too
insights.detail: The WNBA's Indiana Fever share Gainbridge Fieldhouse with the Pacers, and Caitlin Clark's arrival made them a national draw. Indiana high school girls' basketball has deep history too.
insights.implication: Plan co-ed and women's-first hoops product for Indianapolis from the start.

places.name: Hinkle Fieldhouse
places.why: The state's basketball shrine and a National Historic Landmark. Home to Butler, and host of the 2026 NBA Cup championship on Dec 11.

places.name: Gainbridge Fieldhouse
places.why: Home of the Pacers and the Fever, and the pro hub of the market.

places.name: Crispus Attucks High School
places.why: Oscar Robertson's school, and the first all-Black school to win the Indiana state title.

places.name: Assembly Hall
places.why: Indiana University's home, with its banners and the Bob Knight era mythology.

places.name: Mackey Arena
places.why: Purdue's court, the other half of the state's college divide.

places.name: New Castle Fieldhouse
places.why: One of the largest high school gyms in the country, and a symbol of small-town Hoosier Hysteria.

places.name: Indiana Basketball Hall of Fame
places.why: The state's official shrine to high school and Hoosier hoops history.

places.name: Indiana State's Hulman Center
places.why: Where Larry Bird's Sycamores became a statewide story.

people.name: Oscar Robertson
people.why: The Attucks legend and a symbol of Black Indianapolis basketball pride.

people.name: Larry Bird
people.role: Hall of Fame forward, former Pacers coach and executive
people.why: From French Lick and Indiana State, he is the state's most-claimed hoops icon.

people.name: Reggie Miller
people.why: Not a native, but adopted as the franchise's defining figure.

people.name: Tyrese Haliburton
people.why: The current face of the team, and a comeback story.

people.name: Rick Carlisle
people.why: A Pacers coach with a championship pedigree, trusted by locals.

people.name: Caitlin Clark
people.why: Turned the Fever into a national phenomenon.

people.name: Mike Conley Jr.
people.why: A Lawrence North product, part of the state's modern high school lineage.

people.name: Eric Gordon
people.why: An Indianapolis native and North Central High School star.

vocabulary.meaning: The statewide basketball fervor, especially around the high school tournament.
The annual award for the state's top senior, treated as local royalty.
Local shorthand for Gainbridge or Hinkle, depending on context.

Local self-description of politeness. It reads as a cliche if overplayed.

designCues.use: Accent. Keep it distinct from Purdue old gold.
A warm brick-red accent for a gym-heritage capsule.
Line art of arched rafters on tees and warm-ups, with institutional permission.
Varsity block lettering and chenille-style patches for team-adjacent apparel.

designCues.source: Maple hardwood of the state's gyms
designCues.use: A subtle grain print on the lining or outsole.
A restrained "back" narrative for guard product that doesn't trivialize the injury.

productHooks: Hinkle-week capsule: warm-ups, tees and a cream-and-brick colorway tied to the Dec 11 NBA Cup final, subject to Butler licensing.
Fieldhouse-heritage tee and hoodie series with rafter line art and varsity block type, aimed at small-town Indiana gyms.
Guard-focused signature push built on Haliburton's return, coordinated with his athlete agreements.
Women's hoops product tied to the Fever at Gainbridge, designed with and for women players.
watchouts: Crispus Attucks and other community institutions are partners to credit, not an aesthetic to borrow.
College marks (Indiana, Purdue, Butler, Notre Dame) and the Hoosiers film are third-party IP. License them.
Skip the Indiana-nice and corn-and-farm caricature. The state's basketball culture is also urban, and part of Black Indianapolis history.
Player likeness, including Haliburton's injury story, needs athlete approval.
